links_touching_record.rationale: The SOA design record's interfaces field is a signal table naming fault_request as bool and violation_details as a struct at event rate. FB2-SW-IFS-000002 replaces it with the four declared elements of the module, three of which return void and register diagnosis events, and the fourth of which is declared and called on the 10 ms cycle and does nothing. It refines FB2-SW-DSN-000002 and sits alongside FB2-SW-DSN-000005, which designs the debounce internally and still carries no interface contract.

The second specification FB2-SW-SIR-000001 is derived from. FB2-SW-SIR-000001 covers the acquisition and monitoring boundary and its derivation field names every interface specification it came from; this link names the second one so that a reader following the requirement to its evidence reaches both specifications rather than only the first. The direction and the reason are the same as for the first specification: the specification establishes what the interface is by analysing the source, and the requirement states what must be true of it.

consuming_modules.consumption_evidence: All four are called from one block inside BMS_Trigger, at src/app/application/bms/bms.c L913, L914, L915 and L916 respectively, each passing the module's own database entries. The block is guarded by a test that the state machine is not uninitialised, at L911.
consuming_modules.name: BMS_Trigger, the battery-management state-machine trigger

consuming_modules.consumption_evidence: Every outcome of every implemented element is a DIAG_Handler call, for example DIAG_Handler(DIAG_ID_CELL_VOLTAGE_OVERVOLTAGE_MOL, DIAG_EVENT_NOT_OK, DIAG_STRING, s) at src/app/application/soa/soa.c L90.
consuming_modules.name: DIAG module, the diagnosis consumer of the side effects

concurrency.evidence: Reached only through BMS_Trigger, which runs in the 10 ms cyclic task of priority FTSK_TASK_CYCLIC_10MS_PRIORITY = OS_PRIORITY_HIGH at src/app/task/config/ftask_cfg.h L106. No interrupt context reaches this entry point in the source.
concurrency.protection_mechanism: None at this boundary. The function writes diagnosis state through DIAG_Handler, whose own protection this record does not cover.

error_paths.observed_behaviour: A precondition assertion trips at the first statement of the body.

error_paths.condition: The undervoltage MSL threshold is reached and deep discharge is also indicated.
error_paths.observed_behaviour: The return value of DIAG_Handler for the MSL event is captured and, only when it equals DIAG_HANDLER_RETURN_ERR_OCCURRED and the voltage is at or below BC_VOLTAGE_DEEP_DISCHARGE_mV, a further DIAG_ID_DEEP_DISCHARGE_DETECTED event is registered.
error_paths.signalled_as: DIAG_HANDLER_RETURN_ERR_OCCURRED, observed inside the module and not returned

not_specified_by_source: The interface does not state the voltage unit it expects in the struct. The values it compares are read as mV by the comparison against BC_VOLTAGE_MAX_MOL_mV and its siblings, which are (2720), (2750), (2800), (1580), (1550) and (1500) in src/app/application/config/battery_cell_cfg.h L135-L180, so the unit is inferable from the configuration rather than declared by the interface.

The interface does not state the number of strings it iterates. It loops s from 0 to BS_NR_OF_STRINGS, which is (1u) at src/app/application/config/battery_system_cfg.h L109, so a corpus configured for more strings would need this interface re-read rather than trusted.
The interface returns nothing, so a caller cannot tell whether a violation was detected from this call. The only way to know is to inspect diagnosis state afterwards, and no such rule is stated here.

The interface does not state whether the diagnosis threshold is reached before the event is raised. The debouncing is inside DIAG_Handler, whose threshold is configuration, and this interface says nothing about it.

parameters.range_evidence: FAS_ASSERT(pMinimumMaximumCellVoltages != NULL_PTR) at src/app/application/soa/soa.c L82 is the only range this interface states.

return_contract.default_on_no_information: Not applicable as a return value, and that is itself the contract weakness: the function reports nothing to its caller. Its only output is the side effect of registering diagnosis events with the DIAG module.
return_contract.evidence: Declared void in the source; the interface communicates entirely through side effects.

timing.evidence: The period is imposed by the caller, and the caller is on a fixed task: SOA_CheckVoltages is called at src/app/application/bms/bms.c L913 inside BMS_Trigger, BMS_Trigger is called from FTSK_RunUserCodeCyclic10ms at src/app/task/config/ftask_cfg.c L280, and FTSK_TASK_CYCLIC_10MS_CYCLE_TIME is 10u at src/app/task/config/ftask_cfg.h L112.

The function's whole effect is a sequence of DIAG_Handler calls, for example DIAG_Handler(DIAG_ID_CELL_VOLTAGE_OVERVOLTAGE_MOL, DIAG_EVENT_NOT_OK, DIAG_STRING, s) at src/app/application/soa/soa.c L90. A caller learns the outcome only by later reading the diagnosis state, not from this call.
validity_signalling.mechanism: Side effect: diagnosis events registered through DIAG_Handler. No return value exists.

concurrency.evidence: Reached only from BMS_Trigger at src/app/application/bms/bms.c L914, in the 10 ms cyclic task.

error_paths.observed_behaviour: A precondition assertion trips at the top of the body.

not_specified_by_source: The interface does not state the temperature unit. Like the voltage interface, the unit is inferable from the configuration constants the body compares against and is not declared by the interface.

The interface does not state which of the pack values it uses from pCurrent, nor why a current is needed to judge a temperature. The second parameter is a struct far wider than the judgement requires and the interface does not say which fields are read.
The interface returns nothing and states no outcome.
No threshold, no debounce and no error case beyond the pointer preconditions is stated by the interface; all of it lives in the diagnosis configuration.
